name: Polishing Cloth
desc: A palm-sized fold of soft warm-grey microfibre, bunched in the fist with one corner hangin

problems: The silhouette reads as a mushroom (smooth dome cap on a centred stalk), or as a grey stone or brain. It does not read as a soft bunched cloth. The 'hanging corner' poly sits right under the middle of the mass, so it looks like a stem.
The fold lines are three near-parallel horizontal arcs evenly spaced over the dome. They read as ridges or gills on a hard shell, not as fabric creases gathered into a fist.
The outline is too smooth and symmetric. The 13-point poly is basically an ellipse with no lumps, pinches or puckers where a fist would squeeze it.
The gold line along the lower-left edge reads as a stray band or loose wire and is not tied to any feature. On a microfibre rag it is unmotivated.

The fill (#8a8f96→#5c6168) is a cool metallic grey with glossy white highlight strokes along the top. It reads as brushed metal or stone, not warm-grey soft microfibre. Two highlights that strong make it look hard.
Held views: scale against the hand is fine and it sits at the hand. But at that size it becomes a grey blob with a spike that could be a tool or a small bell, so the cloth identity is lost.

for: the object held while: Tomás rubs a glass prism with a cloth in small circular strokes, leaning toward it, one hand steadying the glass

problems: The picture is mostly a big clenched fist, not a cloth. The fist is drawn like grey stone or marble with gold cracks, so it looks like a statue hand. The cloth is only a small grey flap hanging below it.

Held in the character's hand, the sprite adds a second hand. A giant grey fist sits on top of Tomás's own hand, about as wide as his head, so it reads as a glove or boxing fist rather than a polishing cloth.
Scale is wrong. A palm-sized cloth should be smaller than the character's hand, but the sprite (62x110) is roughly the size of his head and neck together.
Rendering style doesn't match. It is heavily textured and sculpted, not the flat, clean shading of the characters.
At a glance, nothing says 'cloth for polishing': no soft bunched fabric shape you can read as a whole.
